1: # Workshop Calendar integration
2: 
3: ALE-430 and ALE-432 publish regular Workshops and Beginners' Workshops to the
4: committee calendar through one synchronization protocol. ALE-433 adds private
5: Calendar Invitations for newly confirmed regular Workshop places. ALE-434 and
6: ALE-435 use that same participant protocol for Stripe-paid and workshop-credit
7: Beginners' Workshop places. ALE-437 adds a read-only launch preview and explicit
8: activation for existing upcoming eligible attendees.
9: There is no Calendar administration screen.
10: 
11: ## Deployment boundary
12: 
13: The integration owns its event/control/recipient tables, with no changes to Workshop
14: payment tables and no source foreign keys. ALE-437 replaces the old pause flag
15: with target-bound activation fields. Apply migrations before running the new code.
16: Deleted sources deliberately leave their Calendar removal obligations behind.
17: 
18: **Sending is inactive by default.** Credentials and deployment alone do not
19: activate it. Set `WORKSHOP_CALENDAR_ENVIRONMENT` to `isolated` or `production`,
20: then explicitly run the matching activation task after review. The durable
21: activation key binds that environment, both calendar IDs, and the OAuth client
22: ID; changing any of them returns sending to inactive until another explicit
23: activation.
24: 
25: The optional runtime credential names are:
26: 
27: - `WORKSHOP_CALENDAR_CLIENT_ID`
28: - `WORKSHOP_CALENDAR_CLIENT_SECRET`
29: - `WORKSHOP_CALENDAR_REFRESH_TOKEN`
30: - `WORKSHOP_CALENDAR_COMMITTEE_ID`
31: - `WORKSHOP_CALENDAR_PARTICIPANT_ID`
32: 
33: `isolated` requires separate credentials and calendars with synthetic data. It
34: is not a production-data sanitizer. Production credentials, resources, and
35: Google acceptance checks are outside this implementation.
36: 
37: Run these only in an authorized operator session:
38: 
39: ```sh
40: cd apps/phoenix
41: mix dhc.workshop_calendar.preview
42: mix dhc.workshop_calendar.activate isolated
43: mix dhc.workshop_calendar.activate production
44: ```
45: 
46: Preview starts only its read dependencies and Repo, not the application or its
47: workers. It emits private JSON containing recipient PII and makes no Google,
48: database or job writes. Activation re-reads and locks the current sources; it
49: never accepts a saved preview as input. Required missing or invalid end/schedule data refuses the
50: entire activation atomically. Missing or invalid recipients remain per-place
51: follow-up and do not stop eligible recipients from being activated.
52: 
53: Provision them using the existing production secret-manager workflow, not checked
54: in configuration. Use a dedicated organizer owning **both** distinct calendars
55: and only `https://www.googleapis.com/auth/calendar.events.owned`. Calendar/ACL
56: administration and domain-wide delegation are not used. The integration does
57: not create calendars or manage sharing.
58: 
59: Share the committee calendar read-only with the Workspace committee group. Keep
60: the participant calendar restricted and unshared with that group. Review public
61: and inherited domain permissions separately: event guest-list flags are not a
62: calendar ACL. Google organizer/Workspace administrators retain privileged access.
63: 
64: ## Beginners' Workshop end-time readiness
65: 
66: Beginners' Workshops require explicit Dublin civil `startTime` and `endTime`
67: when scheduled or rescheduled. The additive column migration accepts unknown
68: (`null`) legacy end times. The follow-up data migration uses the club-approved
69: baseline of **start + six Dublin civil hours** for existing missing values,
70: including historical rows. This is a baseline, not a recovered historical
71: duration. Explicitly recorded end times are never overwritten. Starts at or
72: after 18:00 remain unknown because six hours would cross midnight; overnight
73: sessions are unsupported. Rolling back the data migration preserves values
74: and any later coordinator corrections.
75: 
76: After deployment and before a later Beginners' Workshop Calendar launch, run
77: `mix dhc.beginners_workshops.end_times` (read-only, no Google calls). Inspect
78: `Dhc.BeginnersWorkshops.end_time_report/1` in an authorized operator session,
79: then resolve each remaining upcoming row with the authorized
80: `{:backfill_end_time, workshop_id, %{end_time: "HH:MM"}}` command through
81: `Dhc.BeginnersWorkshops.execute/3`. Backfill changes no cutoff, offer-round,
82: email, or attendance policy. While sending is active, backfill records Calendar
83: intent just like scheduling and rescheduling; it never calls Google inline.
84: 
85: The separate Intake Email data migration adds an `endTime` chip to the six
86: schedule-bearing templates, retaining coordinator copy and existing chips.
87: If there is no start-time chip, it appends an end-time sentence instead. It
88: rechecks the shared 2,000-character worst-case measure before saving: a custom
89: body too close to the limit stops the deployment with its email type and
90: required size, rather than truncating copy or breaking email delivery. Shorten
91: that template in the existing editor and rerun the migration. Rollback keeps
92: the edited bodies; queued emails are not rewritten or resent. Remaining
93: unknown workshop ends render as `TBC`.
94: 
95: ## Ownership and recovery
96: 
97: Workshop operations commit identifier-only synchronization intent alongside the
98: source change. Google runs outside those transactions. The source-owned
99: `Dhc.Workshops.calendar_projection/1` and
100: `Dhc.BeginnersWorkshops.calendar_projection/1` exclude descriptions, participant
101: details, prices and notes. Source kind plus immutable ID distinguish the two
102: contexts even if their IDs match. Calendar content consists of title/status, time, venue and an
103: ordinary authenticated dashboard URL. Committee events have no guests and all
104: mutations use `sendUpdates=none`. Beginners' Workshops appear on scheduling,
105: independent of offers or payments, using the protected workshop Manage URL.
106: Their owner converts both Dublin civil times through Club Calendar. An unknown
107: or invalid legacy end never becomes a guessed duration or a malformed Google
108: event: it is reported without contacting Google. A source schedule correction
109: re-arms only this data failure, not a terminal Google/authorization failure.
110: 
111: The worker and five-minute repair pass share `Dhc.WorkshopCalendar.sync/3`.
112: Event identities and recreation generations are persisted before creation;
113: uncertain success is recovered by reading the same organizer event. Updates and
114: deletions use Google ETags. An event lease and source revision fence local
115: acknowledgments. Interrupted ownership expires after two minutes. Repair also
116: finds deleted-source work and missed wake-ups.
117: 
118: A persisted create checkpoint distinguishes an event never requested from an
119: insert that may still arrive after timeout. Never-requested deletions settle
120: locally. A 404 after a prepared create stays in repair until a tombstone or
121: successful delete proves that a late insert cannot leave a live event behind.
122: 
123: Temporary failures back off from 30 seconds and exhaust after six attempts.
124: Permanent or exhausted event failures retain their reason and episode and report
125: to Sentry. An episode is claimed under lock; best-effort capture follows commit,
126: never an uncommitted synchronization transaction. Sentry is monitoring, not a
127: guaranteed delivery ledger. Repair does not repeatedly call Google for terminal
128: failures; do not delete integration rows to retry, because that discards identity and cleanup
129: obligations. There is no pause/resume or manual recovery command. Domain commands
130: remain available with missing Google credentials or inactive sending.
131: 
132: Archival does not change Calendar. Cancellation retains the committee event at
133: its scheduled time, marked Cancelled; a cancelled source that was never published
134: does not acquire a new event at launch. Hard deletion removes the organizer event,
135: including after its end. First publication, detail repair and missing-event
136: recreation stop at the exact event end; owed cancellation/deletion still runs.
137: Early Beginners' Workshop attendance finalisation does not cancel, remove or
138: shorten its committee event; its scheduled end remains the publication cutoff.
139: 
140: ## Participant invitations
141: 
142: Regular Workshop payment completion captures the saved Registration address in
143: the same transaction that confirms the new place. Member addresses come from the
144: member snapshot, not PaymentIntent receipt/payer details. External addresses are
145: the participant details saved on the Registration; the legacy Checkout
146: `customer_email` fallback still supports booking identity but never fills a
147: missing participant snapshot or Calendar address. Pending Registrations,
148: unfinished Checkout and compensating payments do not qualify. Replayed payment
149: completion never captures another entitlement or selects a newer profile address.
150: 
151: Beginners' Workshop Stripe completion and workshop-credit confirmation capture
152: the locked Waitlist entry's recorded address only when the Intake actually
153: becomes paid. The person's Intake-link confirmation and the coordinator's
154: confirmation use the same command; it records the binding after applying the
155: credit in that transaction. Held credit and contacted places alone do not qualify,
156: and refused or repeated confirmations record no new entitlement. The retained
157: binding belongs to the integration, keyed by the Intake's immutable ID; neither
158: the Intake nor a delayed worker keeps/chooses another email snapshot. The
159: Checkout payer, frozen hold email and Guardian are not recipient sources.
160: Payment replays and repeated credit confirmations leave that binding unchanged.
161: Offers, open holds, failed or unpaid Checkout, policy failures and payments
162: refunded after the place closed do not create invitation entitlements. Google
163: failures cannot undo confirmation.
164: 
165: Beginners' Workshop Settlement rows record `:remove_calendar_place` for deferral,
166: withdrawal, cancel-with-refund and workshop cancellation alongside their existing
167: effects. Refund submission/completion is independent. Attendance finalisation and
168: corrections deliberately have no removal step, even when a no-show is corrected
169: to deferred: that is attendance history, not a prospective place withdrawal.
170: `calendar_place_ids/1` therefore reports confirmation facts (`paid_at`), including
171: historical Intakes; a retained binding's explicit removal obligation determines
172: place loss. This read never selects recipients or creates new entitlements.
173: Reschedule uses the same participant event, preserving surviving Google RSVPs.
174: Recipient failures retain one durable episode per failed place and report to
175: Sentry; they do not create capability/dashboard Notifications.
176: 
177: The integration retains each logical place and its selected address separately
178: from source storage, including failed addresses and owed removals. The shared
179: `sync/3` operation takes `audience: :participant`; identifier-only jobs include
180: that audience. Event identity/generation, leases, retries and failure episodes
181: are the same protocol as committee synchronization. Participant events have an
182: independent identity on the restricted calendar and contain only title, explicit
183: start/end and venue, plus Google event/guest metadata. Guests cannot see other
184: guests, edit the event or invite others. No dashboard links or descriptions are
185: exported.
186: 
187: Cancellation and refund requests record removal when the place ends, not when
188: Stripe completes its refund. Whole-workshop cancellation deletes the participant
189: event while retaining the Cancelled committee entry. Reconciliation reads Google
190: before replacing the attendee array and preserves surviving guest records/RSVPs.
191: Removals run before isolated additions; malformed or Google-rejected addresses
192: remain per-place follow-up and cannot block valid invitations. Terminal recipient
193: failures report to Sentry once per durable failure episode. No-op reconciliation is
194: silent; privacy-only repair does not notify guests. New invitations, meaningful
195: detail changes, guest removals and event cancellation use `sendUpdates=all`.
196: 
197: Attendance and archival preserve Calendar history. At/after the scheduled end,
198: there are no first invitations, detail rewrites or missing-event recreations.
199: Owed attendee removals and event cancellation still run. A Google-only RSVP
200: decline or removal of a personal copy is not a lost dashboard place or another
201: invitation entitlement. A new confirmed Registration or Intake after a lost place
202: is a new entitlement, including when loss and reconfirmation happened while sending was inactive.
203: Spending or forfeiting an applied workshop credit during attendance finalisation
204: does not remove historical invitations.
205: 
206: ## Person deletion and historical privacy cleanup (ALE-436)
207: 
208: The existing Beginners' Workshop manual Delete and three-month retention purge
209: capture privacy-removal obligations for every retained Intake binding before
210: anonymising or unlinking the person. They use the same authoritative transaction
211: and locks as before. Authorization, deletion refusals, refunds, anonymisation and
212: reporting are unchanged; Google never runs in that transaction and cannot delay
213: the person's deletion. There is no new Member/Principal deletion policy: those
214: records currently have no supported person hard-delete entrypoint. The shared
215: Calendar boundary accepts source-owned place identifiers for either source kind
216: when a supported operation needs it; it never finds people by matching email.
217: 
218: Obligations live on the integration's retained recipient rows, without source
219: foreign keys. Identifier-only jobs and periodic repair find them even after the
220: Waitlist entry/profile is gone. Inactive sending retains them without Google
221: mutations; activation reconciles current facts, not queued attendee snapshots.
222: Cleanup runs at and after event end, and even with an unknown legacy end time.
223: It removes the retained selected address from current and
224: historical organizer events, preserving other guests, their RSVPs and event
225: details. An address shared by another active entitlement remains that guest's
226: address; deleting one binding must not cancel the other's invitation.
227: 
228: Cleanup uses the event lease/revision and Google's conditional-write ETag. Even
229: when the guest is already absent, a conditional write advances the provider fence
230: before personal data is discarded, preventing an expired worker's late update
231: from restoring it. Ambiguous success is read back through the same bounded retry
232: and Sentry-reporting protocol. A tombstone or an event never requested can
233: settle without creation. A bare 404 after a prepared creation retains the
234: obligation: the uncertain insertion might still arrive. Cleanup never recreates
235: an event solely to remove someone, including after its end.
236: 
237: Once acknowledged under current ownership, cleanup clears the binding's selected
238: address, previous addresses and recipient failure data. It keeps only an inactive,
239: address-free place tombstone so stale confirmation retries cannot select an
240: address again. Event acknowledgments contain no attendee snapshots; jobs contain
241: no addresses or request bodies. A failed historical removal remains outstanding
242: for bounded reconciliation and Sentry reporting.
243: 
244: This cleans integration-owned organizer details only. It cannot guarantee erasure
245: of recipient calendar copies, delivered invitation emails or Google's retained
246: data. Neither successful HTTP responses nor cleanup acknowledgments promise
247: invitation email delivery or universal deletion.
248:

- Use the already included and available `:req` (`Req`) library for HTTP requests, **avoid** `:httpoison`, `:tesla`, and `:httpc`. Req is included by default and is the preferred HTTP client for Phoenix apps

### Phoenix v1.8 guidelines

- **Always** begin your LiveView templates with `<Layouts.app flash={@flash} ...>` which wraps all inner content
- The `MyAppWeb.Layouts` module is aliased in the `my_app_web.ex` file, so you can use it without needing to alias it again
- Anytime you run into errors with no `current_scope` assign:
  - You failed to follow the Authenticated Routes guidelines, or you failed to pass `current_scope` to `<Layouts.app>`
  - **Always** fix the `current_scope` error by moving your routes to the proper `live_session` and ensure you pass `current_scope` as needed
- Phoenix v1.8 moved the `<.flash_group>` component to the `Layouts` module. You are **forbidden** from calling `<.flash_group>` outside of the `layouts.ex` module
- Out of the box, `core_components.ex` imports an `<.icon name="hero-x-mark" class="w-5 h-5"/>` component for hero icons. **Always** use the `<.icon>` component for icons, **never** use `Heroicons` modules or similar
- **Always** use the imported `<.input>` component for form inputs from `core_components.ex` when available. `<.input>` is imported and using it will save steps and prevent errors
- If you override the default input classes (`<.input class="myclass px-2 py-1 rounded-lg">)`) class with your own values, no default classes are inherited, so your
custom classes must fully style the input


<!-- usage-rules-start -->

<!-- phoenix:elixir-start -->
## Elixir guidelines

- Elixir lists **do not support index based access via the access syntax**

  **Never do this (invalid)**:

      i = 0
      mylist = ["blue", "green"]
      mylist[i]

  Instead, **always** use `Enum.at`, pattern matching, or `List` for index based list access, ie:

      i = 0
      mylist = ["blue", "green"]
      Enum.at(mylist, i)

- Elixir variables are immutable, but can be rebound, so for block expressions like `if`, `case`, `cond`, etc
  you *must* bind the result of the expression to a variable if you want to use it and you CANNOT rebind the result inside the expression, ie:

      # INVALID: we are rebinding inside the `if` and the result never gets assigned
      if connected?(socket) do
        socket = assign(socket, :val, val)
      end

      # VALID: we rebind the result of the `if` to a new variable
      socket =
        if connected?(socket) do
          assign(socket, :val, val)
        end

- **Never** nest multiple modules in the same file as it can cause cyclic dependencies and compilation errors
- **Never** use map access syntax (`changeset[:field]`) on structs as they do not implement the Access behaviour by default. For regular structs, you **must** access the fields directly, such as `my_struct.field` or use higher level APIs that are available on the struct if they exist, `Ecto.Changeset.get_field/2` for changesets
- Elixir's standard library has everything necessary for date and time manipulation. Familiarize yourself with the common `Time`, `Date`, `DateTime`, and `Calendar` interfaces by accessing their documentation as necessary. The one sanctioned date/time dependency is `tz`, the IANA database behind `Dhc.ClubCalendar`'s Europe/Dublin conversions. **Never** install additional dependencies unless asked or for date/time parsing (which you can use the `date_time_parser` package)
- Don't use `String.to_atom/1` on user input (memory leak risk)
- Predicate function names should not start with `is_` and should end in a question mark. Names like `is_thing` should be reserved for guards
- Elixir's builtin OTP primitives like `DynamicSupervisor` and `Registry`, require names in the child spec, such as `{DynamicSupervisor, name: MyApp.MyDynamicSup}`, then you can use `DynamicSupervisor.start_child(MyApp.MyDynamicSup, child_spec)`
- Use `Task.async_stream(collection, callback, options)` for concurrent enumeration with back-pressure. The majority of times you will want to pass `timeout: :infinity` as option

## Mix guidelines

- Read the docs and options before using tasks (by using `mix help task_name`)
- To debug test failures, run tests in a specific file with `mix test test/my_test.exs` or run all previously failed tests with `mix test --failed`
- `mix deps.clean --all` is **almost never needed**. **Avoid** using it unless you have good reason

## Test guidelines

- **Always use `start_supervised!/1`** to start processes in tests as it guarantees cleanup between tests
- **Avoid** `Process.sleep/1` and `Process.alive?/1` in tests
  - Instead of sleeping to wait for a process to finish, **always** use `Process.monitor/1` and assert on the DOWN message:

      ref = Process.monitor(pid)
      assert_receive {:DOWN, ^ref, :process, ^pid, :normal}

   - Instead of sleeping to synchronize before the next call, **always** use `_ = :sys.get_state/1` to ensure the process has handled prior messages
<!-- phoenix:elixir-end -->

<!-- phoenix:phoenix-start -->
## Phoenix guidelines

- Remember Phoenix router `scope` blocks include an optional alias which is prefixed for all routes within the scope. **Always** be mindful of this when creating routes within a scope to avoid duplicate module prefixes.

- You **never** need to create your own `alias` for route definitions! The `scope` provides the alias, ie:

      scope "/admin", AppWeb.Admin do
        pipe_through :browser

        live "/users", UserLive, :index
      end

  the UserLive route would point to the `AppWeb.Admin.UserLive` module

- `Phoenix.View` no longer is needed or included with Phoenix, don't use it
<!-- phoenix:phoenix-end -->

<!-- phoenix:ecto-start -->
## Ecto Guidelines

- **Always** preload Ecto associations in queries when they'll be accessed in templates, ie a message that needs to reference the `message.user.email`
- Remember `import Ecto.Query` and other supporting modules when you write `seeds.exs`
- `Ecto.Schema` fields always use the `:string` type, even for `:text`, columns, ie: `field :name, :string`
- `Ecto.Changeset.validate_number/2` **DOES NOT SUPPORT the `:allow_nil` option**. By default, Ecto validations only run if a change for the given field exists and the change value is not nil, so such as option is never needed
- You **must** use `Ecto.Changeset.get_field(changeset, :field)` to access changeset fields
- Fields which are set programmatically, such as `user_id`, must not be listed in `cast` calls or similar for security purposes. Instead they must be explicitly set when creating the struct
- **Always** invoke `mix ecto.gen.migration migration_name_using_underscores` when generating migration files, so the correct timestamp and conventions are applied
<!-- phoenix:ecto-end -->

<!-- usage-rules-end -->

The one exception: real-Stripe `:integration` suites `put_env` a real `:stripe_secret_key` and reset `:stripe_req_options` to `[]` in setup (and restore both on exit); no other test changes Stripe config. Stubs reach Tasks/inline jobs via `$callers`; other processes need `Req.Test.allow/3`. Shared subscription-payment decoding lives in `Dhc.Stripe.SubscriptionPayment` and the one retry rule in `Dhc.Stripe.Failure.retryable?/1`; see "Stubbing Stripe" in `docs/agents/notes.md`.
- Keep generated Stripe modules under `lib/dhc/stripe/generated/` excluded from Credo instead of refactoring generated source
- Use the already included and available `:req` (`Req`) library for HTTP requests, **avoid** `:httpoison`, `:tesla`, and `:httpc`. Req is included by default and is the preferred HTTP client for Phoenix apps
- **Documented exception (ADR 0021)**: transactional email goes through Swoosh, whose api client is `config :swoosh, api_client: Dhc.Email.ApiClient` wrapping `Swoosh.ApiClient.Finch` over a named `{Finch, name: Swoosh.Finch}` child in `Dhc.Application`. - Hackney is test-only because Testcontainers requires its 1.x Unix-socket transport. Keep it out of production and do not force Hackney 4 until Testcontainers supports Docker Unix sockets with it; the matching Hackney advisory exceptions in `mix.exs` apply only to that test dependency.

### Phoenix v1.8 guidelines

- **Always** begin your LiveView templates with `<Layouts.app flash={@flash} ...>` which wraps all inner content
- The `MyAppWeb.Layouts` module is aliased in the `my_app_web.ex` file, so you can use it without needing to alias it again
- Anytime you run into errors with no `current_scope` assign:
  - You failed to follow the Authenticated Routes guidelines, or you failed to pass `current_scope` to `<Layouts.app>`
  - **Always** fix the `current_scope` error by moving your routes to the proper `live_session` and ensure you pass `current_scope` as needed
- Phoenix v1.8 moved the `<.flash_group>` component to the `Layouts` module. You are **forbidden** from calling `<.flash_group>` outside of the `layouts.ex` module
- Out of the box, `core_components.ex` imports an `<.icon name="hero-x-mark" class="w-5 h-5"/>` component for hero icons. **Always** use the `<.icon>` component for icons, **never** use `Heroicons` modules or similar
- **Always** use the imported `<.input>` component for form inputs from `core_components.ex` when available. `<.input>` is imported and using it will save steps and prevent errors
- If you override the default input classes (`<.input class="myclass px-2 py-1 rounded-lg">)`) class with your own values, no default classes are inherited, so your
custom classes must fully style the input

## Elixir guidelines

- Elixir lists **do not support index based access via the access syntax**

  **Never do this (invalid)**:

      i = 0
      mylist = ["blue", "green"]
      mylist[i]

  Instead, **always** use `Enum.at`, pattern matching, or `List` for index based list access, ie:

      i = 0
      mylist = ["blue", "green"]
      Enum.at(mylist, i)

- Elixir variables are immutable, but can be rebound, so for block expressions like `if`, `case`, `cond`, etc
  you *must* bind the result of the expression to a variable if you want to use it and you CANNOT rebind the result inside the expression, ie:

      # INVALID: we are rebinding inside the `if` and the result never gets assigned
      if connected?(socket) do
        socket = assign(socket, :val, val)
      end

      # VALID: we rebind the result of the `if` to a new variable
      socket =
        if connected?(socket) do
          assign(socket, :val, val)
        end

- **Never** nest multiple modules in the same file as it can cause cyclic dependencies and compilation errors
- **Never** use map access syntax (`changeset[:field]`) on structs as they do not implement the Access behaviour by default. For regular structs, you **must** access the fields directly, such as `my_struct.field` or use higher level APIs that are available on the struct if they exist, `Ecto.Changeset.get_field/2` for changesets
- Elixir's standard library has everything necessary for date and time manipulation. Familiarize yourself with the common `Time`, `Date`, `DateTime`, and `Calendar` interfaces by accessing their documentation as necessary. The one sanctioned date/time dependency is `tz`, the IANA database behind `Dhc.ClubCalendar`'s Europe/Dublin conversions. **Never** install additional dependencies unless asked or for date/time parsing (which you can use the `date_time_parser` package)
- Don't use `String.to_atom/1` on user input (memory leak risk)
- Predicate function names should not start with `is_` and should end in a question mark. Names like `is_thing` should be reserved for guards
- Elixir's builtin OTP primitives like `DynamicSupervisor` and `Registry`, require names in the child spec, such as `{DynamicSupervisor, name: MyApp.MyDynamicSup}`, then you can use `DynamicSupervisor.start_child(MyApp.MyDynamicSup, child_spec)`
- Use `Task.async_stream(collection, callback, options)` for concurrent enumeration with back-pressure. The majority of times you will want to pass `timeout: :infinity` as option

## Mix guidelines

- Read the docs and options before using tasks (by using `mix help task_name`)
- To debug test failures, run tests in a specific file with `mix test test/my_test.exs` or run all previously failed tests with `mix test --failed`
- `mix deps.clean --all` is **almost never needed**. **Avoid** using it unless you have good reason

## Test guidelines

- **Always use `start_supervised!/1`** to start processes in tests as it guarantees cleanup between tests
- **Avoid** `Process.sleep/1` and `Process.alive?/1` in tests
  - Instead of sleeping to wait for a process to finish, **always** use `Process.monitor/1` and assert on the DOWN message:

      ref = Process.monitor(pid)
      assert_receive {:DOWN, ^ref, :process, ^pid, :normal}

   - Instead of sleeping to synchronize before the next call, **always** use `_ = :sys.get_state/1` to ensure the process has handled prior messages
<!-- phoenix:elixir-end -->

<!-- phoenix:phoenix-start -->
## Phoenix guidelines

- Remember Phoenix router `scope` blocks include an optional alias which is prefixed for all routes within the scope. **Always** be mindful of this when creating routes within a scope to avoid duplicate module prefixes.

- You **never** need to create your own `alias` for route definitions! The `scope` provides the alias, ie:

      scope "/admin", AppWeb.Admin do
        pipe_through :browser

        live "/users", UserLive, :index
      end

  the UserLive route would point to the `AppWeb.Admin.UserLive` module

- `Phoenix.View` no longer is needed or included with Phoenix, don't use it
<!-- phoenix:phoenix-end -->

<!-- phoenix:ecto-start -->
## Ecto Guidelines

- **Always** preload Ecto associations in queries when they'll be accessed in templates, ie a message that needs to reference the `message.user.email`
- Remember `import Ecto.Query` and other supporting modules when you write `seeds.exs`
- `Ecto.Schema` fields always use the `:string` type, even for `:text`, columns, ie: `field :name, :string`
- `Ecto.Changeset.validate_number/2` **DOES NOT SUPPORT the `:allow_nil` option**. By default, Ecto validations only run if a change for the given field exists and the change value is not nil, so such as option is never needed
- You **must** use `Ecto.Changeset.get_field(changeset, :field)` to access changeset fields
- Fields which are set programmatically, such as `user_id`, must not be listed in `cast` calls or similar for security purposes. Instead they must be explicitly set when creating the struct
- **Always** invoke `mix ecto.gen.migration migration_name_using_underscores` when generating migration files, so the correct timestamp and conventions are applied
<!-- phoenix:ecto-end -->

<!-- usage-rules-end -->

Added ALE-441 integration coverage in `apps/phoenix/test/dhc/workshop_calendar/beginners_participant_test.exs`.

It exercises public scheduling, fast-track/payment, and destination enrichment with fixed clocks and Req.Test Google/OAuth. It verifies both audiences’ location, separate stable event IDs, participant privacy, RSVP preservation, notification semantics (`all` participant / `none` committee), directions-link exclusion, and no-op reconciliation.

Verified with Colima:
- `mix test test/dhc/workshop_calendar/beginners_participant_test.exs` — 16 passed
- `mix test test/dhc/workshop_calendar` — 140 passed

`mix format --check-formatted` still flags a pre-existing concurrent indentation change at line 226 of the same test file; I did not alter that unrelated line.
